title: The Sweep Year Forfeiture Entry on a Northbeam Circle Membership
content:
## When a sweep falls due

A sweep of aged reward points falls due on the Northbeam Circle Membership itself, and this schedule governs
one figure: the points the sweep forfeits, booked for one sweep year.

## What the booking does to the record

One call lands one forfeiture entry for the sweep year named: the ledger gains a row carrying the points taken
off and the sweep year they belong to, and the reward point balance shown on the membership drops by those
points. The member sees the forfeiture as its own entry, told apart from a redemption, and a lower point
balance.

## How the sweep is booked

`sweep_expired_points_bcca39ef` is the desk's own tool: it is unlocked and then called by the agent handling
the membership.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
|---|---|---|
| membership_id | The reference number of the Circle membership the points are swept from | An identifier, read from the membership record returned when the membership is looked up |
| points_swept | The points taken off the balance | Whole points, signed, passed as a positive whole number with no decimal part and no thousands separator; stored as an integer count of points at exactly that precision, the entry itself carrying it as a reduction |
| expiry_cycle_year | The sweep year this forfeiture belongs to | The four-digit calendar year YYYY, with no month or day part and no other punctuation |

## What comes back

A confirmation line naming the membership, the points taken off, the sweep year the forfeiture belongs to and
the reference number of the new forfeiture entry; the presence of that forfeiture entry reference is what
marks the call as completed.
